01 Getting Started

TAS Simulator is a browser-based tool for planning measurements on neutron triple-axis spectrometers (TAS). It handles accessible momentum and energy regions, instrument angles, resolution, unit conversions, crystal-structure files, and measurement scripts.

This manual was prepared using the public version as verified on October 8, 2026 (UTC). Interface labels are shown as they appear in English. The screenshots were captured and cropped from the public version.

TabMain purpose
Q-E RangeAccessible regions, angle calculations, scans, and measurement-time estimates
ResolutionResolution ellipses and resolution matrix
ToolboxUnit conversion, X-ray-to-neutron angle conversion, and neutron transmission
CIF GeneratorCrystal-structure input, CIF generation, and nuclear-reflection checks
mCIF GeneratorCrystal/magnetic-structure setup, structure display, and mCIF output
ScriptEdit measurement commands, estimate time, and convert SPICE macros

Try a Basic Calculation

  1. Instrument in CTAX@HFIR and select Fixed = Ef、Ef = 4.8 meVConfirm the displayed settings.
  2. Set Sample to Single crystal, space group P1, a = b = c = 5 Å, and α = β = γ = 90°.
  3. Set Scattering plane to U = (1,0,0) and V = (0,1,0).
  4. In Q-E Range → Constant E map, check the accessible region at ħω = 0 meV.
  5. In Angle calculation & TAS geometry → Single below, enter (h,k,l) = (1,0,0) and ħω = 0, then check the angles and geometry diagram.
The example conditions are for demonstrating operation only. After changing the instrument, recheck loaded values such as energy and angle limits. Scroll the settings pane on the left and the work area on the right independently as needed.

02 Instrument & Sample Settings

Instrument Configuration

ItemWhat to set/check
InstrumentSelect the instrument preset. Eight presets were available when this manual was verified.
Fixed / Ei・EfChoose whether to fix the incident energy Ei or final energy Ef, and enter the value in meV. ħω = Ei − Ef.
Geometry / Sense / S1 signW / anti-W, scattering-sense combination, and the S1 rotation sign. Match these to the convention of the actual instrument.
λ/2 (only elastic)Toggle for handling the half-wavelength component under elastic conditions.
S1 min / max、S2 minLower and upper instrument-angle limits, in degrees.
JSON S2 maxS2 upper limit supplied by the preset.
ΔS2 max / Effective S2 maxRelative correction to the upper limit and the corrected upper limit. Editing the Effective value updates ΔS2. For CTAX, the correction is applied to the Ei-dependent limit.

Sample and Scattering Plane

  1. Choose Single crystal or Powder under Type.
  2. Specify Space group # / Space group and the lattice constants. If you have a structure file, load it with Select CIF/mCIF.
  3. For a single crystal, enter independent reciprocal-lattice vectors U and V that span the scattering plane. W is displayed automatically.
  4. Under Sample orientation → Orientation reference, choose ki ⟂ U, ki ⟂ V, ki ∥ U, ki ∥ V, or Bragg peak position to define the sample-orientation reference.

Magnetic Reflections, Background, and Masking

ItemHow to use
Propagation vectorsUse show to toggle display, enter the components of k1, etc., add vectors with + Add propagation vector, and enable or disable each one with its checkbox.
Background scatteringSelect a background material in BG. Al, Cu, Fe, Ti, and W were available when verified; use + Add background to specify multiple materials.
Dark angleEnable show and select the Sample environment. Set Reference, Rotation, and, when needed, the reference Q and From / To / Offset values.
Multiple masksUse + Add range to add an angular range and + Add dark angle to add another masking configuration.
Dark angle options include MAG-I, Horizontal Magnet, and Pressure Cell. Do not rely on the preset name alone; verify it against the orientation and angular opening of the installed sample environment. For powders, use |Q| and S2 rather than a single-crystal HKL scattering plane.

03 Q-E Range: Explore Accessible Regions

Constant E Map: Reciprocal-Space Slice at Fixed Energy

  1. Open Constant E map.
  2. Enter ħω (meV) below the plot or adjust it with the slider.
  3. Switch Q unit between Å⁻¹ and r.l.u. and check whether the desired reflection or Q position lies in the accessible region.
  4. If too many nuclear-reflection labels are shown, clear Display labels of nuclear Bragg peaks.
For propagation vector k1 = (0,0,0), magnetic-reflection markers overlap the nuclear reflections. Check the legend rather than relying on color alone. The accessible region is not a prediction of measured intensity.

Q Vector–E Map: Q Direction vs. Energy

  1. Switch to Q vector–E map.
  2. Enter two points on the reciprocal-space line of interest in HKL 1 and HKL 2.
  3. Check the HKL direction on the horizontal axis, ħω on the vertical axis, and the yellow Accessible Q region. The two selected points are indicated by dashed lines.

Single: Calculate Angles and Geometry for One Point

In Angle calculation & TAS geometry → Single, enter h, k, l, and ħω to display Ei, Ef, |Q|, and M1, M2, S1, S2, A1, and A2. In the geometry diagram, check the relationship among the Monochromator, Sample, Analyzer, Detector, ki, kf, and Q. Set U / Set V and Set ki ⟂ U change the orientation settings, so use them as appropriate.

Scan: Check a Sequence of Measurement Points

  1. Switch to Scan and enter the initial and final HKL and ħω values and the number of Points.
  2. Table to check the angles and StatusConfirm the displayed settings.
  3. Switch to TAS geometry to select a point and inspect its geometry.
Check warnings for invalid scattering triangles, Q points outside the scattering plane, angle limits, masking, and related constraints. Read the Status field rather than judging from table colors alone. A numerical result for a point outside the scattering plane does not necessarily mean that the point is measurable.

Time Estimate

The Time Estimate section below estimates measurement time from the command sequence, MCU values, and related settings. The Script tab uses the same command sequence. See Section 7 for operation details.

04 Resolution: Estimate Instrument Resolution

  1. Open the Resolution tab and choose Cooper-Nathans or Popovici under Approximation.
  2. With Mode = single, enter H, K, L, and ħω for one point. In scan mode, set the start and end points and related values.
  3. Choose r.l.u. or Å⁻¹ under Unit.
  4. Check focusing, collimation, crystal/mosaic, and size settings under Instrument details.
  5. Compare the calculation point, numerical resolution values, and ellipse plots; expand Resolution Matrix if needed.
Setting groupDescription / units
Focusing conditionsHorizontal/vertical focusing and number of blades for the monochromator and analyzer.
Collimator conditions (min)Horizontal and vertical collimation at each position. “min” means arcminutes. When 1st supermirror is enabled, also check the m-value.
Crystal & Mosaic (min)Crystal type and mosaic width. Expand the section to inspect the values.
Component size (m)Dimensions of instrument components, in meters.
Resolution is an estimate that depends on the entered instrument parameters and approximation model. For comparisons, keep the energy, calculation point, units, and focusing conditions consistent. Interpret line styles and numerical definitions according to the labels shown in the interface.

05 Toolbox: Conversions & Transmission

Unit Conversion

Enter a known quantity and the corresponding values are updated. The tool handles wavelength, energy, wave number k, frequency, temperature equivalent, spectroscopic wave number (cm⁻¹), velocity, and related quantities. The table below shows values corresponding to 1/3 λ, 1/2 λ, 2 λ, and 3 λ.

The basic relationships are k = 2π/λ and E ∝ 1/λ². Temperature is the temperature equivalent of the energy; it is not a sample-temperature setpoint.

S2 Conversion

  1. Select a source under X-ray source, or choose Custom and enter the X-ray conditions.
  2. Enter the observed 2θ in Observed X-ray S2 (deg). Multiple angles can also be specified.
  3. Check the value and unit under Neutron beam. To use the current instrument condition, click Set default.
  4. Check d (Å) and Neutron S2 (deg). If the Bragg condition is not satisfied for the neutron beam, review the result and adjust the wavelength or other conditions.
Toolbox inputs do not necessarily reset to identical conditions whenever the instrument is changed. In particular, use Set default for Neutron beam or enter the intended value directly.

Neutron Attenuation

  1. Choose Manual or CIF/mCIF under Input mode.
  2. In Manual mode, enter Chemical formula and Density (g/cm³). In CIF/mCIF mode, select a structure file with Select CIF/mCIF.
  3. Enter Energy / Wavelength, Sample thickness (mm), and, if needed, SE transmission (%).
  4. Check the material information and transmission output. Overall transmission (%) represents transmission including the sample environment.

SE means sample environment. Chemical formula, density, thickness, and wavelength affect the result, so check for blank fields and unit mistakes.

06　CIF / mCIF Generator

CIF Generator: Create a Crystal-Structure File

  1. Open CIF Generator and set the Space group and lattice constants. Use Copy current lattice to copy the lattice from the common settings.
  2. Under Atomic positions, enter the element, fractional coordinates x, y, z, and Occupancy. Add independent sites with + Add atom or + Copy atom.
  3. Check energy, wavelength, and k under Reflection parameters. Set default uses the current instrument energy.
  4. Generate and click CIF preview and Reflection tableConfirm the displayed settings.
  5. Save with Download CIF. To apply the generated structure to the simulator sample, click Set CIF. Save the reflection table with Download table.
In this example, two atoms were generated from one independent site by symmetry operations. Do not enter symmetry-equivalent atoms repeatedly as independent sites. Generate and Set CIF are separate operations.

Using the Reflection Table

Use Reflection table to inspect nuclear-reflection indices, intensity, multiplicity, scattering angle, Q, d, and related values. If no reflections are found, check the space group, structure, and wavelength conditions. In this Fe example, the CTAX setting of 4.8 meV (about 4.128 Å) is too long even for the first (110) reflection, so the wavelength condition must be reconsidered when checking whether a reflection can be observed.

mCIF Generator: Configure a Magnetic Structure

  1. Load a CIF, or create one in CIF Generator and click Set CIF, then open mCIF Generator.
  2. Under View, use a/b/c or a*/b*/c* and the x/y/z min/max values to specify the viewing direction and range.
  3. Use Atoms / Spins / Bonds to switch display and structure settings.
  4. Under Spins, choose the propagation vector and Structure type (Collinear / Helical / Sinusoidal). Under Direction, choose Cartesian or Polar and enter the magnetic moment for each site.
  5. After Generate, check mCIF preview, save with Download mCIF when it becomes available, and apply it with Set mCIF.

In Structure, use the unit cell, XYZ axes, atom legend, Save figure, and related controls. Distinguish a magnetic structure loaded from mCIF from one newly defined in the interface, and verify the atomic and magnetic information in the generated text.

Verification-environment limitation:The browser used for verification displayed “WebGL is not supported,” so correct rendering of the 3D structure and the mCIF generation result could not be verified. The screenshot in this section shows the settings area. Verify the 3D view and mCIF output in an environment with WebGL support.

07 Script: Measurement Sequences & SPICE Macros

Script consists of three areas: ASET (auxiliary-control templates), Time estimate commands (command sequence), and SPICE macro. On narrow screens, use Hide ASET to widen the command area and scroll horizontally within tables.

Create Commands

  1. Command and Target and select Details and enter values or ranges.
  2. Add a row with + Add scan or duplicate one with + Copy scan. Row numbers are used for selection and reordering.
  3. For commands with counting conditions, set MCU and related values. Use the on-screen ⓘ Info for input instructions.
  4. Convert the command sequence to a macro with → SPICE. Check the result and use Copy to copy it out.
  5. To start from an existing compatible macro, enter it under SPICE macro and convert it with ← Commands.
CommandPurpose
drive / driverelMove to a specified value / relative move
scan / scanrelAbsolute / relative scan
scantitleSet the measurement title
count / waitCount / wait
loop1, etc.Repetition. Check Info for loop ranges and expressions.

Estimate Measurement Time

Set 1 MCU = … s, Movement time (%), and the conditions for each command. Use Set now to set the start time and Calc finish to calculate the finish time. When using Calc MCU, check the start/end times and which items are fixed. Behavior changes depending on fixed rows and input errors, so read the messages in the results area.

ASET: Auxiliary Control for Temperature, Field, etc.

Add a target with + Add ASET and define an instrument-appropriate command in the SPICE template. Follow the Info instructions for placeholders such as <value> and <range>. The ASET template is expanded during → SPICE conversion.

Conversion between the command sequence and SPICE text is performed explicitly with the conversion buttons. After changing one side, run the conversion again. Before using a generated macro, verify device names, motion limits, and sample-environment control procedures against the actual instrument.
